children: The move will increase borrowing costs for existing and new external benchmark-linked loans as banks reprice lending rates

Several domestic banks have raised their repo-linked lending rates by 25 basis points (bps) after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increased the policy repo rate to 5.5 per cent. The move is set to increase borrowing costs for customers with loans linked to external benchmarks.

Bank of Baroda (BoB), Punjab National Bank (PNB), Indian Bank, Indian Overseas Bank (IOB), Bank of India (BoI) and RBL Bank have revised their benchmark-linked lending rates following the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) decision. The revisions will affect both new borrowers and existing customers whose loans are linked to external benchmarks.

BoB has raised its Baroda Repo Based Lending Rate by 25 bps to 8.15 per cent from 7.90 per cent. With the repo rate now at 5.5 per cent, the revised rate represents a spread of 2.65 percentage points over the RBI’s policy rate.

PNB has increased its repo-linked lending rate to 8.35 per cent from 8.10 per cent. Indian Bank has raised its Repo-Linked Benchmark Lending Rate to 8.20 per cent from 7.95 per cent, with the revised rate effective October 8.

IOB has also increased its repo-linked lending rate by 25 bps to 8.35 per cent from 8.10 per cent. BoI has raised its Repo-Based Lending Rate to 8.35 per cent from 8.10 per cent, while RBL Bank’s repo-linked lending rate stood at 8.50 per cent as of October 7.

UCO Bank has revised several benchmark-linked rates with effect from October 8. Its three-month Benchmark Lending Rate (BLR) has increased to 5.30 per cent from 5.25 per cent, while the six-month Treasury Bill Linked Rate (TBLR) has risen to 5.70 per cent from 5.55 per cent.

The bank has raised its 12-month TBLR to 5.95 per cent from 5.70 per cent. Its one-year government securities-linked rate has increased to 6.26 per cent from 5.88 per cent, while the 10-year Gsec-linked rate has moved up to 7.32 per cent from 7.09 per cent.
UCO Bank has also raised the repo-linked rate for UCO Float to 8.30 per cent from 8.05 per cent. The repo-linked rate for UCO Prime has been increased to 5.50 per cent from 5.25 per cent.

For new loans linked to external benchmarks such as the repo rate, the 25-bps increase will be transmitted immediately through the applicable lending rate. Existing external benchmark-linked loans will also be repriced upwards by a similar amount, typically within 90 days.

The impact on deposit rates is expected to emerge more gradually. Banks currently have additional liquidity from foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR(B)) deposits, which could reduce the immediate pressure to increase rates across their existing deposit base.
However, banks may offer higher rates on fresh deposits if short-term money market rates remain elevated. This could gradually increase funding costs as banks seek to attract new deposits.

The lending rate revisions follow Wednesday’s MPC decision to raise the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5 per cent. The six-member panel unanimously supported the rate increase, which was broadly in line with market expectations.

The bigger policy shift came through the change in stance from “neutral” to “calibrated tightening”. Four MPC members supported the change, while external members Ram Singh and Nagesh Kumar favoured retaining the neutral stance.

RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated a hawkish outlook, stating that rate cuts were off the table in the near term. He said future policy action could involve either a rate hike or a pause, depending on evolving economic conditions and the outlook.
